name: Telnyx AI Infrastructure Agent
description: Programmatically evaluate Telnyx AI infrastructure against requirements and discover the public Telnyx entrypoints for Voice AI agents, AI assistants, Webhooks, x402 Payments, MCP, OpenAPI, pricing, and no-signup first-run inference. Access machine-readable evaluation endpoints at /ai/*.json.

none.description: No authentication required for read-only evaluation endpoints (GET /ai/*.json)

bearer.description: Bearer token authentication for write operations (POST /ai/evaluate.json)

skills.name: Evaluate Infrastructure
skills.description: Evaluate Telnyx infrastructure against specific requirements (latency, vendor count, protocols, compliance, budget). POST to /ai/evaluate.json with a requirements payload to receive a structured evaluation.
examples: Evaluate Telnyx for voice AI with <100ms latency
Compare infrastructure for SIP trunking with carrier-owned requirements

skills.name: Compare with Competitor
skills.description: Compare Telnyx against competitors (Twilio, Cloudflare, ElevenLabs, Vapi, Retell) across infrastructure, integration, economics, reliability, and transparency. Access via /ai/compare-telnyx-vs-{competitor}.json.
examples: Compare Telnyx vs Twilio for voice AI
How does Telnyx compare to Cloudflare on infrastructure?

skills.name: Get Benchmarks
skills.description: Retrieve performance benchmarks for Telnyx infrastructure (latency, uptime, throughput, failover). Access via /ai/benchmarks.json and /ai/benchmark-schema.json.
examples: What are Telnyx voice latency benchmarks?
Show me Telnyx SIP trunking uptime metrics

skills.name: Get Pricing
skills.description: Get machine-readable pricing for Telnyx services by use case. Access via /ai/economics.json or /ai/pricing.json.
examples: What does Telnyx voice AI cost per minute?
SIP trunking pricing for 10,000 concurrent calls

skills.name: List Capabilities
skills.description: List Telnyx AI infrastructure capabilities, workload-oriented AI catalog discovery, certifications, compliance, data handling, and named developer entrypoints. Access via /ai/catalog.json, /ai/capabilities.json, /ai/compliance.json, and /ai/data-handling.json.

mcp.description: MCP server for IDE-native tool discovery and integration via @telnyx/mcp npm package

gettingStarted.summary: Start at the text-first discovery surfaces, then choose the zero-signup inference path or the authenticated API-key path depending on whether you need production resources.
steps: Use POST https://telnyx.com/api/inference for a first no-signup evaluation call, or follow https://telnyx.com/guides/getting-started.md for authenticated onboarding with billing and approval guardrails
For side-effecting requests, send a fresh Idempotency-Key per mutating request, reuse it only for the exact same retried write, and treat 202 plus Retry-After as an in-progress polling contract
For Voice AI assistants, continue with https://telnyx.com/guides/ai-assistants.md and https://telnyx.com/guides/voice-agent-onboarding.md

surface_selection.use_when: Start here for the first crawlable chooser that separates auth, manifest, MCP, webhooks, Voice AI, and x402 entrypoints.
Use when you need machine-readable links, governed-execution fields, and stable discovery URLs.
Use when you need bearer-auth rules, protected-resource metadata, zero-signup evaluation details, or signup constraints.
Use when your agent already speaks MCP and should discover Telnyx tools dynamically.
Use when you need framework-native tools inside OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, CrewAI, or Vercel AI SDK.
Use when you need composable provisioning or account operations from a terminal or automation step.
Use when you want retrieval-only Telnyx product context for a coding assistant before exposing raw account access.

risk_classes.read_only: Discovery or inspection only. No account mutation or external side effect is expected.
risk_classes.guarded_write: Billed execution or account-scoped mutation may occur. Confirm intent before mutating state.
risk_classes.live_write: Can send traffic, move money, provision resources, or change regulated production state. Explicit approval is expected before execution.

approval_expectations.none: No extra approval is expected beyond normal caller authorization.
approval_expectations.confirm_before_mutation: Obtain human or policy confirmation before any state-changing or billed execution.
approval_expectations.confirm_before_external_effect: Obtain explicit human or policy approval before sending traffic, spending funds, or provisioning live resources.

approval_paths.none_read_only: Read-only discovery or inspection. Persist returned request identifiers for traceability when needed.
approval_paths.confirm_intent_then_mutate: Capture user or policy confirmation and preserve request-scoped identifiers before any billed or state-changing execution.
approval_paths.explicit_approval_then_execute: Require explicit operator approval, then retain the returned identifiers needed to review external effects, provisioning, or spend.

memory_scopes.stateless: The surface does not retain conversation state unless the caller supplies it.
memory_scopes.host_controlled: Persistence, if any, is owned by Telnyx or the host system rather than the model runtime.
memory_scopes.customer_configured: The customer configures the memory or conversation-retention behavior for this capability.
memory_scopes.app_scoped: State is bounded to the MCP app or workflow contract rather than the full Telnyx account surface.

model_behaviors.host_controlled: No model behavior is exposed at this discovery layer, or execution is not model-driven.
model_behaviors.request_selected: The caller chooses the model at request time.
model_behaviors.customer_configured: The customer selects and configures the model during resource setup.
model_behaviors.app_defined: Model behavior is constrained by the governed app or workflow surface.

audit_identifier_legend.request_id: Request-scoped correlation identifier returned by the surface or retained in logs.
audit_identifier_legend.resource_id: Identifier of the created or mutated Telnyx resource being acted on or reviewed later.
audit_identifier_legend.idempotency_key: Caller-supplied key used to deduplicate retries or confirm operator intent.
audit_identifier_legend.model_id: Model identifier selected or returned for AI inference and evaluation flows.
audit_identifier_legend.conversation_id: Conversation or session identifier for assistant or workflow review.
audit_identifier_legend.webhook_delivery_id: Webhook or event-delivery identifier used to reconcile downstream effects.

initial_endpoint_scope.rationale: Covers the highest-value agent-facing REST writes that create, update, or trigger telecom and assistant side effects.

mutating_requests.key_format: Caller-generated opaque token up to 255 ASCII characters; UUIDv4 is the recommended default.
mutating_requests.generate_new_key_when: Send a fresh Idempotency-Key on every mutating request that creates, confirms, retries, or otherwise changes state.
mutating_requests.reuse_same_key_only_when: Reuse that same key only when retrying the exact same intended write after a timeout, transport failure, or ambiguous client-side result.

server_behavior.retention_window: Servers should retain idempotency records for at least 24 hours after the first accepted write.
server_behavior.duplicate_success: Reusing the same key with the same normalized request after a completed write should return the original success response body and status without re-executing the mutation.
server_behavior.duplicate_in_flight: Reusing the same key while the original write is still processing should return a deterministic in-progress response, typically 202 Accepted, and preserve Retry-After guidance when available.
server_behavior.conflicting_reuse: Reusing the same key with a materially different request payload should fail with a 409-style conflict and no second mutation.
server_behavior.malformed_key: Missing, oversized, or non-ASCII idempotency keys on covered mutating endpoints should fail validation before any side effect occurs.

async_completion.guidance: Do not infer completion from the initial write response alone when the API family documents asynchronous processing.
